walkthroughs.body_html:
The nutrient cycle here is fast.

Warm wet conditions mean leaf litter decomposes quickly, releasing nutrients.

Most nutrients sit in biomass, not the soil, so clearing trees leaves the land poor.

Trees show clever adaptations.

Drip tips shed heavy rain; buttress roots support tall trunks; lianas climb to reach light.

Form follows the hot, wet, crowded environment.

Deforestation has many drivers.

Main causes: cattle ranching, soya, logging, mining and road building.

Once trees go, heavy rain leaches the thin soils and the cycle collapses.

mcqs.q: Why are rainforest soils surprisingly thin?
options: Cold slows decay
Most nutrients are stored in biomass, not soil
There is little rainfall
Soils are mostly sand from the coast

mcqs.q: Which adaptation helps rainforest leaves shed heavy rain?
options: Waxy needles
Drip tips
Spines
Hairy surface

mcqs.q: Why does the tropical rainforest have distinct vertical layers?
options: Rainforest layers exist because trees grow in age order tallest to shortest.
Rainforest layers exist because different animals live at different heights.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
Competition for light: emergents (40m+), canopy (capturing most light), understorey (shade-tolerant) and forest floor (sparse vegetation due to low light) — each adapted to its light level.

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils typically infertile?
options: Because so much vegetation grows there, the soil must be fertile.
Heavy rainfall leaches nutrients, and most nutrients are stored in living biomass and rapidly recycled — the soil itself holds very little.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
Rainforest layers exist because trees grow in age order tallest to shortest.

mcqs.q: Why do tropical cyclones only form over warm tropical oceans?
options: Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
Hurricanes form wherever there are strong winds over the sea.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
They need sea surface temperatures above ~27 degrees C to a depth of 50m to provide energy through evaporation, plus enough Coriolis effect (away from the equator) to spin.
